what: The CB reference never states that a CB page capacity must be an EXACT MULTIPLE of every push/pop quantum used on it. dataflow_api.h:216-221 only wraps fifo_wr_ptr/fifo_rd_ptr when it lands exactly on fifo_limit (comment: no other wrap is legal); the guarding ASSERT is compiled out in default builds AND under run_safe_pytest.sh --dev (TT_METAL_WATCHER_DISABLE_ASSERT=1). Violating it is silent: an indexed multi-tile window straddles the ring boundary and reads/writes past the CB. Cost me a full hang plus a block-width restructure. grep over all of .claude/references/ for fifo_limit / multiple-of-quantum returns nothing.
suggest: Add a CB SIZING RULE section to ttnn-cb-memory-fundamentals.md: capacity_pages % quantum == 0 for EVERY distinct push and pop count on that CB, with the dataflow_api.h:216-221 citation, a note that the ASSERT is off under --dev, and the two shapes that break it in practice: (a) a ragged per-core work split against a uniform CB capacity, (b) any Upfront/indexed window whose size does not divide capacity.

what: The Python-bindings reference lists no cross-core primitives at all: ttnn.Mcast2D / ttnn.Mcast1D / ttnn.McastConfig (bound in ttnn/cpp/ttnn-nanobind/mcast_host.cpp), ttnn.SemaphoreDescriptor, and device.worker_core_from_logical_core are all callable from Python but absent from the doc. Any Python ProgramDescriptor op with a multicast or gather needs every one of them. An initial grep for Mcast2D outside kernel_lib/host found only C++ gtests, which reads as not exposed to Python; I only recovered the wire via ttnn/ttnn/operations/examples/tensix_all_reduce/program_descriptor_with_inline_kernels.py.
suggest: Add a Cross-core / multicast section to ttnn-python-utility-bindings.md covering McastConfig(noc=, handshake=, sem_ids=), Mcast2D(device, rect, sender, cfg) with .compile_time_args()/.runtime_args(core)/.owned_semaphores(), SemaphoreDescriptor(id=, core_ranges=, initial_value=), and worker_core_from_logical_core, and point at the tensix_all_reduce example as the worked call site.

what: The public L1Accumulation enum carries a one-line comment on the enum itself (whether a pack adds DEST to the output tile already in L1) and NO comment on the Enabled value. The load-bearing constraint is only in eltwise_chain.inl:1007-1017: walk is forced false whenever L1AccumulationMode != Disabled, so the pack is PINNED to a single output tile and cannot accumulate into N distinct tiles unless TileOffset::Strided supplies the index (which in turn forces caller-managed (None,None) policies). The op design prescribed an L1Accumulation::Enabled pack into a per-tile-row accumulator, which is simply not expressible that way; I had to read the .inl to find out and redesign the stat-CB layout.
suggest: Document on the L1Accumulation enum in the public header: Enabled/SeedFirst pin the pack to ONE output tile (walk is disabled); to accumulate into several tiles, pair it with TileOffset::Strided and caller-managed (None,None) reserve/push. Same note belongs on the PackTile alias.

what: The L1 budget is specified as device.l1_size_per_core() - L1_RESERVE_BYTES, but l1_size_per_core is not exposed on the Python device object (dir(ttnn.MeshDevice) has compute_with_storage_grid_size and dram_grid_size, no L1 size query). A Python ProgramDescriptor op must therefore hardcode an arch->L1-size table keyed off ttnn.get_arch_name(), which is exactly the kind of inlined constant the blocking-model rules forbid elsewhere.
suggest: Either bind l1_size_per_core() (or a ttnn.l1_size_per_core(device) free function) for Python, or have l1-footprint-discipline.md state the sanctioned Python fallback so every op does not invent its own arch table.
